questions.prompt: Complete the JavaScript functions turnOn() and turnOff() to control the light bulb. In turnOn(), set the bulb (#bulb) background color to gold (or yellow) and change status (#status) text to 'Light is ON'. In turnOff(), set the bulb background color back to gray and change status text to 'Light is OFF'.
questions.code:
Smart Light Bulb

Light is OFF

answerText.c-1: Use count++; (or count += 1;) inside the while loop so each digit increments the count.
answerText.c-2: Define #define DOUBLE(x) ((x)*4) (or call DOUBLE(18) / use x*4) so the result evaluates to 36.
answerText.c-3: Initialize min = a[0]; so the minimum tracks from an existing array element.
answerText.c-4: Use char s[6] = "world"; to leave room for the terminating null character '\0'.
answerText.c-5: Pass by pointer: void addTwo(int *x) { *x += 2; } and invoke addTwo(&a);.
answerText.dsa-1: Change the loop boundary to i < n / 2 so elements are swapped only once.
answerText.dsa-2: Change the comparison to if (a[j] > a[j + 1]) to swap adjacent elements out of order.
answerText.dsa-3: Update bounds with low = mid + 1; and high = mid - 1; to avoid infinite loops when missing.
answerText.dsa-4: Check if (top == -1) (or top < 0) before popping to catch the Underflow condition.
answerText.dsa-5: Save next = cur->next; before reversing cur->next = prev;, then advance cur = next;.
answerText.python-1: Create an independent copy using b = a.copy() (or b = list(a) or b = a[:]).
answerText.python-2: Initialize independent sublists using a list comprehension: grid = [[1] * 2 for _ in range(3)].
answerText.python-3: Check for even numbers using if n % 2 == 0:.
answerText.python-4: Declare global points inside increase() to modify the outer variable.
answerText.python-5: Map student name to marks: marks[name] = 60 + i * 10.
answerText.dbms-1: Remove unaggregated column: SELECT dept, COUNT(*) FROM employees GROUP BY dept;.
answerText.dbms-2: Use a subquery: SELECT name FROM employees WHERE salary < (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees);.
answerText.dbms-3: Add the missing comma: SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE salary > 45000;.
answerText.dbms-4: Use IS NULL to find missing values: WHERE email IS NULL;.
answerText.dbms-5: Filter grouped aggregates with HAVING: GROUP BY dept HAVING AVG(salary) > 50000;.
